analysis: All supplied units are test-only Swift files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Autopilot: three new test suites (SelectedModelRecoveryPolicyTests, SelectedModelRecoveryTests, SelectedModelRecoveryVictimTests) and a fixture change to UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture.swift. The fixture change adds a ScriptedCounter class, a superLoads counter, a residentBytes switch with a case for Super, and an instrumented stub Super loader that always throws. No production source is changed here, so there is no runtime change to the attack surface, key handling, attestation, WebSocket, cache encryption or fan helper. Relevant threat IDs: T-059 and T-060 (add-on hold) and A-018 serving availability. The tests assert the following behavior of the production recovery feature, whose implementation is not in this batch: eviction respects holds, leases, pins, minimum dwell, idle time, requests in flight, and models in the running daemon's selection. An add-on hold cancels an in-progress recovery load. Checks pause while the provider is draining or busy. Non-memory refusals end the recovery. These tests encode good safety properties, but the production code in ProviderLoop, SelectedModelRecovery and related files was not supplied. Whether it enforces them, for example the hold-cancels-load fence from T-059 or eviction not racing with request admission, is unverified. Temp directories are created under FileManager.temporaryDirectory and removed. The test code touches no real secrets or network (the coordinator URL is ws://127.0.0.1:0/unused). Integration should check the production recovery implementation if included in another batch, particularly eviction authority, the add-on hold interaction, and that the unload path cannot evict models serving requests.
